description: The single-wrap vs typed nucleon-NF counit gap is h^3(h^4+2h^3+2h^2+2h-1)/4, leading -h^3/4, so the two NFs agree through O(h^2) and the gap contributes nothing at order t^1 or t^2. It therefore cannot move the qou-pdix entry-6 branch-3 acceptance test, which pins at t^1 and predicts t^2. Separately: because the Frobenius counit is a canonical (basis-independent) map, two expansions of ONE element cannot give different eps, so the 1.00579 factor is NOT a 'basis-change' as labelled in the 2026-05-11 audit - the two NFs expand DIFFERENT ELEMENTS. That audit's own section 2 proves the net IS the counit, which is what makes the section 1 label a category error against it.

checks.name: gap_vanishes_to_order_three

checks.name: the_two_eps_differ
checks.why: different polynomials => (eps canonical) => DIFFERENT ELEMENTS, not two bases for one element

checks.name: gap_has_no_t1_term
checks.why: the NF gap contributes nothing at order t^1 — so it cannot move the entry-6 acceptance test

checks.name: gap_has_no_t2_term
checks.why: the NF gap contributes nothing at order t^2 — so it cannot move the entry-6 acceptance test

checks.name: gap_first_appears_at_t3
checks.why: first nonzero order in t is 3

data.verdict: The NF ambiguity is O(h^3) = O(t^3) and does NOT gate the entry-6 acceptance test. The bean's magnitude argument (0.579% vs a 0.160% target) is untouched and still correct for the ABSOLUTE target; a magnitude at q0 and an order in the expansion are different claims.
